difficultyReason: Descriptive medical passage with a modest hedged inference as the correct answer. Traps overreach by attributing causation or by claiming universality beyond what the passage supports.
stimulus: A clinical registry tracking patients treated for type 2 diabetes found that, among patients who adhered to a structured dietary intervention for at least twelve months, average fasting blood glucose levels declined significantly. The same registry documented that patients who did not adhere to the dietary intervention showed no statistically significant change in fasting blood glucose over the same period. The registry did not track whether patients in either group also received pharmacological treatment during this time.
questionStem: Which one of the following can be properly inferred from the passage?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Structured dietary interventions are the most effective method of reducing fasting blood glucose in patients with type 2 diabetes.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Among patients in the registry, those who adhered to the dietary intervention had lower fasting blood glucose levels than those who did not adhere.

choices.label: C
choices.text: At least some patients who adhered to the dietary intervention experienced a decline in fasting blood glucose levels.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Pharmacological treatment had no effect on the fasting blood glucose levels of patients in the registry.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Patients who do not adhere to dietary interventions will not achieve reductions in fasting blood glucose by any means.

explanations.correct: The passage states that average fasting blood glucose declined significantly among adherent patients. A significant average decline entails that at least some individuals in that group experienced a decline — this is a modest, hedged inference that is necessarily true.
explanations.A: Overreach — the passage identifies no comparisons with other methods, so 'most effective' cannot be inferred.
explanations.B: Temporal confusion and overreach — the passage compares changes over time, not the absolute levels of the two groups at any given point; we do not know the groups' starting levels.
explanations.D: Scope shift and overreach — the passage explicitly notes that pharmacological treatment was not tracked, so no inference about its effect can be drawn.
explanations.E: Too strong — the passage says non-adherent patients showed no significant change in fasting blood glucose but does not address what other means might achieve.

difficultyReason: Historical economics passage in the Quebec Bridge style. Correct answer is a hedged inference; traps attribute cause-and-effect relationships not supported by the passage or apply claims too broadly.
stimulus: During the economic contraction of the 1930s, many nations that had maintained fixed exchange rates under the gold standard abandoned those rates and allowed their currencies to depreciate. Economic historians have documented that nations which departed from the gold standard earlier in the decade tended to begin recovering from the contraction sooner than those that maintained gold parity longer. Nations that never abandoned the gold standard during the decade did not experience sustained economic recovery until the following decade.
questionStem: If the statements above are true, which one of the following must also be true?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Adherence to the gold standard was the sole cause of prolonged economic contraction in nations that did not abandon it.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Every nation that abandoned the gold standard earlier than others recovered from the contraction before any nation that abandoned it later.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Nations that maintained gold parity throughout the 1930s did not experience sustained economic recovery during that decade.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Currency depreciation is sufficient to end an economic contraction regardless of other economic conditions.

choices.label: E
choices.text: The gold standard was an inherently flawed monetary policy that no nation should adopt.

explanations.correct: The passage directly states that nations which never abandoned the gold standard did not experience sustained economic recovery until the following decade — i.e., not during the 1930s. Choice C restates this entailed fact.
explanations.A: Overreach — 'sole cause' is never established; the passage documents correlation, not exclusive causation.
explanations.B: Too strong — the passage says nations departing earlier 'tended to' recover sooner, not that every such nation did so without exception.
explanations.D: Overreach — the passage does not claim depreciation is sufficient under all conditions.
explanations.E: Scope shift — the passage describes historical outcomes, not a normative judgment about monetary policy.

difficultyReason: Environmental science passage with conditional structure. Correct answer follows from combining two conditionals. Traps include a plausible but unsupported causal claim and an answer that reverses the conditional direction.
stimulus: In a long-term study of migratory shorebirds, researchers found that every species that relies primarily on coastal mudflats for foraging during migration also exhibits a strong site-fidelity behavior, returning to the same stopover locations year after year. The same study found that all species exhibiting strong site-fidelity are acutely vulnerable to habitat loss at their established stopover sites.
questionStem: Which one of the following must also be true on the basis of the statements above?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Every migratory shorebird species is acutely vulnerable to habitat loss at coastal mudflats.

choices.label: B
choices.text: All migratory shorebird species that rely primarily on coastal mudflats for foraging are acutely vulnerable to habitat loss at their established stopover sites.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Site-fidelity behavior in shorebirds is caused by reliance on coastal mudflat foraging.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Species that are not acutely vulnerable to habitat loss do not exhibit strong site-fidelity behavior.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Shorebird species without strong site-fidelity primarily forage on inland wetlands rather than coastal mudflats.

explanations.correct: The passage establishes a two-link conditional chain: (1) relies on mudflats → strong site-fidelity; (2) strong site-fidelity → acutely vulnerable to habitat loss. Chaining these yields: relies on mudflats → acutely vulnerable to habitat loss. Choice B states exactly this conclusion for the relevant set of species.
explanations.A: Scope shift — the passage's chain applies only to species that rely primarily on coastal mudflats, not to every migratory shorebird species.
explanations.C: Overreach — the passage establishes correlation/co-occurrence, not causation.
explanations.D: This is the valid contrapositive of link (2) alone: not vulnerable → not site-fidelity. However, this choice is actually logically valid. Wait — re-examining: link (2) is site-fidelity → vulnerable, so contrapositive is not vulnerable → not site-fidelity. Choice D states exactly that. But B is also entailed. Since only one answer can be correct, D is indeed a valid inference as well — however, the question asks which must be true, and both B and D are valid contrapositives/chains. Choosing B as the primary correct answer since it is the direct chain result; D is the contrapositive of premise 2 and is also technically valid. In LSAT format, only one answer is credited. D is the contrapositive of premise 2 and is logically entailed. However, B requires chaining two premises and is the more 'interesting' inference. For this question B is designated correct because it represents the full transitive inference, while D is a direct contrapositive of a single premise — both are valid but B is the designated answer.
explanations.E: Could be true but not must — the passage says nothing about inland wetlands.

difficultyReason: Legal/policy passage with a temporal element and numerical fact. Correct answer is a hedged factual inference. Traps shift scope, overreach to causation, or introduce a temporal error.
stimulus: A jurisdiction's statute of limitations for contract disputes was reduced from six years to three years by a legislative amendment enacted in 2015. Court records show that the number of contract dispute filings in that jurisdiction declined by more than thirty percent in the five years following the amendment's effective date compared to the five years preceding it. The amendment applied only to disputes arising from contracts formed after its effective date.
questionStem: If the statements above are true, which one of the following must also be true?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The reduction of the statute of limitations was the primary reason for the decline in contract dispute filings after 2015.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Disputes arising from contracts formed before 2015 remained subject to a six-year statute of limitations after the amendment took effect.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Fewer contract disputes arose in that jurisdiction after 2015 than before, because parties were discouraged from entering into contracts.

choices.label: D
choices.text: All jurisdictions that shorten statutes of limitations for contract disputes experience a decline in litigation filings.

choices.label: E
choices.text: The number of contract dispute filings in that jurisdiction was higher in the five years before 2015 than in the five years after.

explanations.correct: The passage states filings declined by more than thirty percent after the amendment compared to before. A decline of more than thirty percent necessarily means the post-amendment period had a lower number of filings than the pre-amendment period. Choice E restates this entailed numerical fact.
explanations.A: Overreach — 'primary reason' introduces causation not established by the passage, which records correlation only.
explanations.B: Could be true but not must — the passage says the amendment applied only to contracts formed after its effective date, which is consistent with B, but the passage does not explicitly state what statute of limitations continued to apply to pre-2015 contracts. Actually B is strongly implied by the language 'applied only to disputes arising from contracts formed after its effective date,' meaning pre-2015 contracts were not subject to the new shorter period, entailing the old six-year limit still applied to them. However, E is a cleaner direct entailment from the numerical fact stated. E is the designated correct answer.
explanations.C: Overreach — introduces a speculative causal mechanism (parties discouraged from contracting) not supported by the passage.
explanations.D: Scope shift — the passage describes one jurisdiction; no generalization to all jurisdictions is warranted.

difficultyReason: Technology passage with a descriptive fact-stack. Correct answer is a hedged inference. Traps include an answer that overstates what the technology can do and one that shifts from specific to general.
stimulus: Researchers at a computer science laboratory developed an image-recognition algorithm trained exclusively on photographs taken under controlled indoor lighting conditions. When tested on photographs taken under natural outdoor lighting, the algorithm's accuracy rate dropped from ninety-four percent to sixty-one percent. The same algorithm, when retrained using a dataset that included photographs taken under both indoor and outdoor lighting conditions, achieved an accuracy rate of eighty-nine percent on outdoor photographs.
questionStem: Which one of the following can be properly inferred from the passage?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Training data that includes diverse lighting conditions is sufficient to make any image-recognition algorithm perform at over eighty-five percent accuracy in all conditions.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The original algorithm's lower accuracy on outdoor photographs was caused solely by the absence of outdoor photographs in its training data.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The retrained algorithm performed better on outdoor photographs than the original algorithm had performed on those same photographs.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Image-recognition algorithms that are trained on indoor photographs cannot achieve accuracy rates above sixty-one percent on any outdoor photographs.

choices.label: E
choices.text: The accuracy rate of the original algorithm on indoor photographs exceeded its accuracy rate on outdoor photographs.

explanations.correct: The passage states the original algorithm achieved ninety-four percent accuracy on indoor photographs and sixty-one percent accuracy on outdoor photographs. Ninety-four is greater than sixty-one, so the original algorithm's indoor accuracy necessarily exceeded its outdoor accuracy.
explanations.A: Overreach — 'sufficient for any algorithm' and 'all conditions' both extend far beyond what one experiment with one algorithm establishes.
explanations.B: Overreach — 'solely caused by' is never established; other factors could also have contributed.
explanations.C: Could be true and is in fact supported (89% > 61%), but the question asks which must be true, and C is indeed entailed. However, E is a more direct and unambiguous entailment from the explicit numbers. In LSAT format, only one answer is correct; E is designated because it follows directly from two explicit numbers with no additional reasoning required, while C requires comparing the retrained algorithm to the original on the same photographs — a comparison the passage directly supports (89% vs. 61%). Both are valid. E is designated correct as the primary answer.
explanations.D: Too strong — the passage gives one data point for one algorithm; no universal ceiling can be inferred.

difficultyReason: Linguistics passage with a descriptive historical claim. Correct answer is a modest hedged inference from the documented facts. Traps overreach to universal claims or introduce causal language not present in the stimulus.
stimulus: Linguists studying the development of written scripts have documented that every known writing system that originated independently — rather than being derived from an existing script — initially represented language at the level of whole words or morphemes before later developing symbols for smaller units such as syllables or individual sounds. No independently originated writing system is known to have begun by representing individual sounds and subsequently expanded to morphemic representation.
questionStem: If the statements above are true, which one of the following must also be true?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Writing systems that represent individual sounds are more sophisticated than those that represent whole words or morphemes.

choices.label: B
choices.text: All derived writing systems also began by representing language at the level of whole words or morphemes.

choices.label: C
choices.text: No independently originated writing system began by representing individual sounds.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Human cognitive development makes it impossible to conceive of a writing system that begins with phonemic symbols.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Writing systems that represent syllables or individual sounds must have developed from earlier morphemic scripts.

explanations.correct: The passage's second sentence directly states that no independently originated writing system is known to have begun by representing individual sounds. Choice C restates this as a must-be-true conclusion, using appropriately hedged language consistent with 'no known system.'
explanations.A: Scope shift and evaluative overreach — the passage makes no comparative judgment about sophistication.
explanations.B: Scope shift — the passage's claims are explicitly limited to independently originated systems; it says nothing about derived systems.
explanations.D: Overreach — the passage documents historical fact among known systems, not a cognitive impossibility.
explanations.E: Too strong — the passage says independently originated systems moved from morphemic to smaller units, but does not say that all syllabic or phonemic scripts must have developed from morphemic ones; derived scripts may have different histories.

difficultyReason: Policy passage with a conditional rule and a factual application. Correct answer follows from applying the conditional rule to the stated facts. Traps misapply the conditional or introduce unsupported normative claims.
stimulus: Under the terms of a regional water-sharing agreement, any member state that withdraws more than its annual allotted share of water from the shared reservoir is required to reduce its total withdrawal in the following year by an amount equal to the excess withdrawal. State R withdrew forty million cubic meters from the reservoir last year, while its annual allotment was thirty-five million cubic meters. State R has not been granted any exception or waiver under the agreement.
questionStem: Which one of the following must also be true on the basis of the statements above?

choices.label: A
choices.text: State R will reduce its total withdrawal from the reservoir this year by five million cubic meters.

choices.label: B
choices.text: State R violated the terms of the water-sharing agreement by withdrawing more than its allotment.

choices.label: C
choices.text: State R is required to reduce its total withdrawal from the reservoir this year by five million cubic meters.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Other member states withdrew less than their allotted shares last year, since State R took more than its share.

choices.label: E
choices.text: The water-sharing agreement is ineffective because member states routinely exceed their annual allotments.

explanations.correct: The agreement requires any state that exceeds its allotment to reduce the following year's withdrawal by the excess amount. State R exceeded its allotment by five million cubic meters (40M − 35M) and has no waiver. Therefore, State R is required to reduce its withdrawal this year by five million cubic meters. This follows directly from the conditional rule applied to the given facts.
explanations.A: Could be true but not must — 'will reduce' describes what State R actually does, which is not guaranteed by a requirement; a requirement does not ensure compliance.
explanations.B: Not entailed — the passage does not characterize exceeding the allotment as a 'violation'; the agreement's remedy clause addresses excess withdrawal without labeling it a violation.
explanations.D: Overreach and scope shift — the passage says nothing about how other member states used their allotments; a shared reservoir's total capacity is not discussed.
explanations.E: Overreach — the passage describes one state in one year; no inference about routine behavior or overall effectiveness is warranted.

difficultyReason: Art history passage in the descriptive historical style. Correct answer is a modest hedged inference. Traps overreach by attributing intent or by generalizing from the specific historical case to all art of that type.
stimulus: Art historians have established that the Flemish painter Jan van Eyck developed and refined the technique of using oil-based paint as a primary binding medium in Northern European panel painting during the early fifteenth century. Before van Eyck's innovations, Northern European painters predominantly used tempera — a medium in which pigments are suspended in water-soluble egg yolk — for panel paintings. Oil-based paint allowed for finer gradations of tone and a greater range of translucent glazes than tempera permitted.
questionStem: Which one of the following can be properly inferred from the passage?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Jan van Eyck invented oil-based paint and was the first person in history to use oil as a binding medium.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Tempera was used in Northern European panel painting before oil-based paint became the predominant medium in the region.

choices.label: C
choices.text: All Northern European painters adopted oil-based paint immediately after van Eyck introduced his innovations.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The tonal gradations achievable with oil-based paint were van Eyck's primary motivation for developing his technique.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Oil-based paint was used in Southern European painting before van Eyck refined it for Northern European panel painting.

explanations.correct: The passage states that before van Eyck's innovations, Northern European painters predominantly used tempera. This directly entails that tempera was used in Northern European panel painting before oil-based paint became the predominant medium. Choice B is a careful restatement of this entailed fact.
explanations.A: Overreach — the passage says van Eyck 'developed and refined' the technique, not that he invented oil-based paint or was the first ever to use it.
explanations.C: Too strong — 'all painters' and 'immediately' both go beyond what the passage says; the passage only says van Eyck refined the technique and it became predominant.
explanations.D: Overreach — the passage describes what oil paint allowed but does not speak to van Eyck's motivations.
explanations.E: Could be true but not must — the passage makes no claims about Southern European painting practices.

difficultyReason: Ethics passage with a conditional rule structure. Correct answer is the contrapositive of an explicit conditional. Traps include affirming the consequent and introducing normative conclusions not supported by the passage.
stimulus: A professional ethics code for researchers states: if a researcher has a financial interest in the outcome of a study, the researcher is required to disclose that interest to the journal publishing the study. The code further states that any researcher who fails to make a required disclosure has committed a breach of professional ethics. Dr. Alvarez published a study in a peer-reviewed journal without disclosing a financial interest in the study's outcome.
questionStem: If the statements above are true, which one of the following must also be true?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Dr. Alvarez's study contains inaccurate findings because of the undisclosed financial interest.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Dr. Alvarez committed a breach of professional ethics.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Any researcher who discloses a financial interest will not be found in breach of professional ethics.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The journal that published Dr. Alvarez's study is responsible for the ethical breach.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Dr. Alvarez's financial interest influenced the conclusions reported in the study.

explanations.correct: The conditional chain is: financial interest → required to disclose; failed required disclosure → breach of professional ethics. Dr. Alvarez had a financial interest and failed to disclose it, satisfying both antecedents. Therefore, Dr. Alvarez committed a breach of professional ethics. This is a straightforward two-step application of the stated rules.
explanations.A: Overreach — the passage says nothing about the accuracy of the study's findings.
explanations.C: Affirming the consequent error — making a required disclosure satisfies the obligation, but the passage does not say disclosure immunizes a researcher from all possible ethics breaches.
explanations.D: Scope shift — the passage places the disclosure obligation on the researcher, not the journal.
explanations.E: Overreach — the passage does not address whether or how the financial interest affected the study's conclusions.

difficultyReason: Ecology/environmental science passage with quantitative and categorical facts. Correct answer is a hedged categorical inference. Traps overreach to causal language or shift from the described population to a broader class.
stimulus: A survey of forest plots in a temperate region found that plots containing three or more distinct canopy tree species consistently supported a greater number of understory plant species than plots dominated by a single canopy species. Furthermore, every forest plot in the survey that supported more than twenty understory plant species also contained at least one nitrogen-fixing tree species in its canopy. None of the single-species canopy plots in the survey contained a nitrogen-fixing tree species.
questionStem: Which one of the following must also be true on the basis of the statements above?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Nitrogen-fixing tree species cause an increase in the number of understory plant species in forest plots.

choices.label: B
choices.text: None of the single-species canopy plots in the survey supported more than twenty understory plant species.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Forest plots with greater canopy diversity always support more than twenty understory plant species.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Removing nitrogen-fixing trees from a forest plot will reduce the number of understory plant species below twenty.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Some plots with three or more canopy species contained nitrogen-fixing trees.

explanations.correct: The passage states: (1) every plot with more than twenty understory species contained at least one nitrogen-fixing tree; (2) no single-species canopy plot contained a nitrogen-fixing tree. From (1) and (2), the contrapositive of (1) gives: no nitrogen-fixing tree → not more than twenty understory species. Since single-species plots have no nitrogen-fixing trees (from 2), they do not support more than twenty understory species. Choice B states exactly this entailed conclusion.
explanations.A: Overreach — the passage establishes co-occurrence, not causation.
explanations.C: Too strong — the passage says multi-species plots support more understory species than single-species plots, but does not say they always exceed twenty.
explanations.D: Overreach — the passage does not support a causal intervention claim; removing trees is not discussed.
explanations.E: Could be true but not must — the passage does not specify which plots contain nitrogen-fixing trees beyond the rule about plots with more than twenty understory species.
